workflow: Pick tasks from the top of the queue (or a page job, to do everything on one page at once). Pages marked held changed recently and are being measured: leave their titles, descriptions and copy alone (adding markup or links to them is fine).
Write the exact change: new title/description, the sentence with the link, the markup fields, the redirect. Use only facts already on the page.
Get approval from the communications team before changing the live site. Merges, archiving and anything sitewide always need approval.
If you have Drupal admin access, make TRPL-owned changes yourself using the recipe. Content changes to a page can be saved as a draft first.
For FiveJars-owned tasks, write a Basecamp to-do: what's wrong, example URLs, the ready-to-paste JSON-LD or setting, how to check.
Check the live page afterwards (view source for meta tags and JSON-LD; follow redirects with curl).
Log each change in config/changes.yml (date, page, kind, what) so the next run holds the page and reports before/after numbers.

recipes.meta: Edit the node (/node/NID/edit) > 'Customize meta tags'. Basic tags: Page title '<title> | [site:name]' (page part 60 characters or fewer) and Description (120-155 characters). Set Open Graph og:title/og:description and Twitter card title/description to match. Save with 'Save' (keeps the moderation state). If the save seems to do nothing, look for a validation error further down the form.
recipes.h1_missing: Open the page's Layout (/node/NID/layout). Make sure the top section shows the page title block (Content fields > Title), which renders as the H1; or change the first heading in the top text block to Heading 1. Save layout.
recipes.h1_multiple: Open the Layout. Keep one H1 (normally the page title block). In any text block whose heading is set to Heading 1, change it to Heading 2. Save layout.
recipes.chain: Configuration > Search and metadata > URL redirects: find the redirects for this address and point the first one straight at the final page. Update any links on the site that use the old address.
recipes.canonical: Edit the node > 'Customize meta tags' > Advanced > Canonical URL: clear it (Drupal then uses the page's own address) or set it to the live page it should point to.
recipes.headings: Open the Layout. In the text blocks, change the heading levels so they step down one at a time (H2 under the page title, H3 under an H2). Headings used just for size should be styled text instead.
recipes.deep: Link to the page from its section's hub page or a related, well-visited page, so people (and crawlers) reach it in three or four clicks.
recipes.alias: Edit the node > URL alias: give it a readable path that fits its section; save. The /node/NID address keeps working and the sitemap will list the readable one. (The lasting fix is FiveJars keeping unaliased /node/ URLs out of the XML sitemap.)
recipes.sitemap: This sitemap URL redirects to another page. Edit the old node > XML sitemap > Inclusion: Excluded, or archive the node if it's retired (a 301 stays in place).
recipes.thin: Only for pages people find in Google. Add useful, verified copy from the page's own subject (what it is, why it matters, what to do next, links to related pages). Never invent facts; draft for review.
recipes.link: Open the source page's Layout. Edit the text block that contains the context sentence and turn the [[bracketed]] words into a link to the target path (relative, e.g. /tr/tr-shot). Don't write new sentences just to hold a link. Save the block, then Save layout.
recipes.orphan: Add 2-3 links to this page from the pages listed under 'link from' (each has the sentence and words to link).
recipes.related: These two pages cover the same subject without linking to each other. Add one natural link each way, in the paragraph where the shared subject comes up.
recipes.duplicate_topic: Two pages compete for one subject. Pick the stronger page (clicks, depth), move anything unique onto it, then archive the other and add a 301 from its alias and /node/NID. Get approval first; draft before publishing.
recipes.redirect: Configuration > Search and metadata > URL redirects > Add redirect: From = broken path, To = target, 301. If Drupal warns the path looks valid, submit again. Bulk: import redirects.csv. Also fix the link on the source page when the target is known.
recipes.via_redirect: Edit the link on each source page so it points straight at the final address.
recipes.schema_article: Edit the node > 'Customize meta tags' > Schema.org Article: @type Article; headline = the page title; description = the meta description; about = Theodore Roosevelt; author and publisher = the Library; dateModified = [node:changed:html_datetime]. Don't paste raw JSON-LD into a text block (it's stripped).
recipes.schema_person: Edit the node > 'Customize meta tags' > Schema.org Person: name, description, image, and sameAs (Wikipedia/Wikidata only when verified).
recipes.schema_event: Edit the node > 'Customize meta tags' > Schema.org Event: name, startDate/endDate (ISO 8601 with a colon in the offset, e.g. 2026-12-04T18:00:00-06:00), location = the Library, offers (price, ticket URL) only from the page.
recipes.striking: Open the page and make it the best answer to that exact search: use the search's words in the title or a heading, answer it plainly in the first paragraph, add the specifics people want (facts already on the site), and link to it from 2-3 related pages. Don't rewrite a page that already ranks in the top 3 for its main search.
recipes.outreach: Read the page. If it's a list of things to do or a travel guide that names nearby attractions, find the author or the update/contact link and ask to be added, with a two-sentence blurb (what the Library is, why it's worth the stop, about 3 1/2 hours) and a photo. Draft the note for approval; nothing goes out without it.

acceptedAnswer.text: You can make a secure online payment through the website: trlibrary.com/donate . Or, send a check payable to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library Foundation to: TR Library 401 E Main Ave Ste 201 Bismarck, ND 58501.

mainEntity.name: IF I JOIN A BENEFACTOR SOCIETY, HOW WILL MY DONATION BE USED?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your donation will provide funding for physical and virtual programing and operations to explore the life, legacy, and enduring relevance of Theodore Roosevelt.

mainEntity.name: MAY I DIRECT MY GIFT TO SUPPORT A SPECIFIC AREA OF TRPL?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most powerful way to support the Library is with an unrestricted gift. Unrestricted support gives us the flexibility to direct resources where the need and opportunity are greatest — such as to the programs, conservation, and educational work that will define the Library's future — and it ensures your generosity has the broadest possible impact. That said, we're always glad to hear from benefactors with a particular passion. If you'd like to support a specific area, we welcome the conversation and would be pleased to explore opportunities that align with your interests and the Library's long-term vision. However you choose to give, your support will be recognized through the appropriate Benefactor Society.

mainEntity.name: WHAT IS THE TAX-EXEMPT STATUS OF THE THEODORE ROOSEVELT PRESIDENTIAL LIBRARY?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library Foundation manages the Library and fundraises on its behalf. The Foundation is a tax-exempt 501(c)(3) organization.

mainEntity.name: WILL MY GIFT BE TAX DEDUCTIBLE?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, gifts are 100% tax-deductible to the full extent of the law.

mainEntity.name: WILL I RECEIVE A TAX RECEIPT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, a tax receipt will be provided.

mainEntity.name: WHAT ARE SOME OF THE BENEFACTOR SOCIETY BENEFITS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Benefits include a special welcome packet, the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library e-newsletter and digital recognition (unless anonymity is requested). Additional opportunities for recognition are available based on level of support.

mainEntity.name: HOW LONG DOES MY BENEFACTOR SOCIETY PARTICIPATION LAST?

acceptedAnswer.text: Benefactor Society participation recognizes the total impact of your cumulative giving.

mainEntity.name: DO YOU SELL OR SHARE BENEFACTOR INFORMATION WITH THIRD PARTIES?
MAY I MAKE AN ANONYMOUS GIFT TO JOIN A BENEFACTOR SOCIETY?

acceptedAnswer.text: Certainly, simply specify your desire to remain anonymous when you make your gift and your request will be honored.

mainEntity.name: WILL MY NAME BE PRINTED IN MATERIALS OR PUBLISHED IN ANY WAY?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, digital recognition (unless anonymity is requested) and additional opportunities for recognition are available based on level of support.
